newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:

Spokesman Peter Guilford said the Commission had requested formal consultations, under the World Trade Organisation dispute settlement procedure, over Japanese pigmeat imports. He said the first session would take place on February 17. He also said Canada was joining the EU in its request.

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said that following Wednesday's Commission meeting, Commissioner Edith Cresson would hold a news conference at 1215/1115 GMT on the fifth framework programme followed by Commissioner Franz Fischler on olive and olive oil at 1245/1145 GMT.

In answer to a question, van der Pas said Luxembourg and Austria had indicated their disagreement with the Commission's decision to autorize genetically modified organisms. He said the Commission was waiting for those countries to present the elements that justified their position.
Van der Pas said he did not expect a decision on taxation of energy products during Wednesday's Commission meeting.
Spokesman Constantin Verros said Spanish Industry and Energy Minister Josep Pique would discuss state aid to Spanish shipyards during his meeting with Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
Verros also said he would be available in the afternoon for a debriefing on British Airways representatives' meeting with Commissioner Van Miert.

Asked about the decision that the Commission would take in order to ensure the restructuring promised by Commission President Jacques Santer to the European Parliament, van der Pas said the Commission would discuss it on Wednesday. He also said it would imply movements of services to DGXXIV.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/102: EU goes to WTO over Japanese pigmeat imports.
- IP/97/105: Future EU/ACP relations: debate over green paper changes speed.
- Speech/97/35: Speech by Commissioner Padraig Flynn on social policy and the economy.
- Provisional agenda of Wednesday's Commission weekly meeting.
